Finally, we do not explicitly limit the quantity of energy shifted during an event and therefore do not constrain pre-cooling to a defined temperature threshold. However, the hourly loss factor and upper shift limit constrain the total amount of pre-cooling that occurs. 2.3.2 Fully dispatchable load model The fully dispatchable load model assumes that a given end-use load is completely flexible over a given time period, as long as the total energy requirement in that given window is met. This model is applied to pumping loads: residential pool and spa pumps and agricultural crop irrigation pumps, as users of these loads are generally thought to be agnostic as to the specific timing of when the pumping occurs. Additionally, we use this model to conduct a high-level analysis of EV flexibility, assuming that drivers are indifferent as to when their vehicle is charged, so long as their total charging needs are met. This model relies on the inputs of baseline hourly electricity demand and hourly price, as well as two key parameters: flex window and maximum power level. The flex window used for the analysis varies by end use, based on the service requirements. Pools are generally required to be pumped daily to maintain water cleanliness, and therefore a 24-hour window is used to ensure daily demand is met. Farms, on the other hand, can typically move irrigation across days, as long as the weekly water needs of the plants are met (Meyers and Hardy 2021), and 12 Draft note: our colleague who helped define this parameter has been OOO while we are finishing the draft; we will add a brief citation/explanation for this assumption in the final report. 14 therefore a 168-hour window is used. Lastly, we use a 72-hour window for EVs, assuming that most drivers do not need to charge their car every day. Note that charging (or pumping) may still occur every day, if demand is high and low prices are occurring across several days - but the model will not require it. Also, it should be noted that the customer must be supplied with a price forecast equal to or longer than the flex window in order for the modeled dispatch to be possible. If prices are only given for one day with no forecast, the customer (and their automation technology) would only be able to make choices on shifting load within that day. The maximum power level represents the highest consumption of the given end use equipment, e.g. the kW rating of the pump or EV charger. This ensures the load is not unreasonably concentrated in low-price hours. For EVs, we set this to 1.2 kW per Level 1 EV, or 7.6 kW per Level 2 EV.
